item.title: Calls for reform to habitual residence condition
item.description: Renewed calls have been made in Leitrim for urgent reform of the habitual residence condition in social welfare law. Cllr Pádraig Fallon told this month's monthly meeting of the local authority, that the clause - a requirement that applicants must show they are genuinely residing in the State, is having a severe impact locally. item.description: In the national football league, following a run of 3 wins, Roscommon seen their hopes of making a league final in Division 1 take a hit when they suffered a defeat to Dublin in Dr Hyde Park on Sunday past. Mark Dowd had made a number of changes to his side from their win over Galway in Rd 4, but noted that you couldn't fault that for what was a flat performance against the visitors Next up Rossies is Donegal on March 15th Advertisement

item.title: Local residents warned of scam
item.description: Residents in the Shannonside region are being warned over a scam. Letters are understood to have been delivered to people’s homes purporting to be from Uisce Éireann and stating that they called to inspect a leak in the property. People are being asked not return any unfamiliar calls or use any QR codes. Advertisement Any suspicious activity can be reported to Carrick-on-Shannon Garda Station on 071 9650510.

item.title: Chartered flight to evacuate Irish citizens from the Middle East
item.description: The Department of Foreign Affairs is working to identify the most vulnerable Irish people currently stranded in the Middle East. It’s planning to bus at least 280 people to Oman, where a chartered flight is set to leave for Ireland later this week. Any vulnerable citizens, including elderly people or those with medical conditions, who have not yet been contacted, are being asked to call the liaison team in Dublin. item.title: 'Unacceptable delays' impact local cancer patients
item.description: Cancer patients across the midlands are facing 'unacceptable delays' when it comes to diagnosis and treatment. That's according to Sinn Féin TD Sorca Clarke who says projections show cancer cancers are set to double by 2045. She says hundreds of patients in the region are waiting beyond recommended timeframes for a colonoscopy and radiation therapy. item.title: Local consumers feeling the pinch at the pumps
item.description: Consumers in the Shannonside region have reported massive hikes in the cost of home heating oil while anxiety surrounds fuel prices at the pumps. Increases of up to 16 cent per litre for motor fuel have been reported following the outbreak of war in Iran. The Irish Road Haulage Association has warned diesel prices are likely to reach and surpass €2 per litre, and has urged the government to introduce temporary supports for operators. item.title: Two hospitalised following north Roscommon crash
item.description: Two men have been hospitalised following a crash in north Roscommon. The two-vehicle collision happened on the R361 between Boyle and Frenchpark at Killaraght at around 4pm. In a statement, Gardai say that both drivers were taken to Sligo University Hospital for assessment. Advertisement There are no other reports of serious injuries and the road has since fully reopened to traffic. An investigation into the collision is ongoing.
